w:r.w:t: Ascend Mobile App Brand Migration Guide
Brand identity, asset use, product copy, technical migration, and release acceptance

The customer-facing brand is Ascend. The mobile app must use Ascend for the app name, visible product language, logo, launcher icon, splash screen, notifications, email references, support screens, and store metadata. Existing Xenoh technical identifiers remain compatible until a coordinated infrastructure migration is approved.

This guide gives the mobile team one implementation reference for the rebrand from Xenoh to Ascend. It defines what users should see, which supplied artwork to use, how to translate the identity into a small mobile icon, and which legacy identifiers must remain stable for compatibility.
Ascend mountain emblem and Ascend wordmark
Ascend references in every supported language
Xenoh namespaces, endpoints, keys, and schemes

Ascend represents measurable progress over time. The mountain and upward A communicate direction, effort, and earned improvement. The circular brush form adds momentum and continuity, reflecting how training records connect one session to the next.
How it should feel in the app
Show the next useful action and make progress easy to understand.
Use recorded training data, clear metrics, and specific recommendations.
Use direct language and strong hierarchy without sounding aggressive.
Keep coaching and recovery language supportive, practical, and respectful.
Reduce visual noise during active workouts and other high-attention tasks.

Use 01 ascend mountain emblem logo for sign-in, registration, account recovery, navigation headers, About screens, and wide marketing placements. It includes the emblem, Ascend wordmark, and the Higher Each Rep tagline.

w:r.w:t: Use 03 golden mountain brush emblem for compact in-app brand marks and as the source concept for the launcher icon. Use 06 monochrome ascend mountain emblem when color is unavailable, including Android themed icon work and single-color production constraints.
Keep the logo proportions unchanged. Never stretch, skew, rotate, or redraw the supplied files.
Leave clear space around the mark equal to at least one quarter of the emblem width.
Use the full lockup only when the wordmark and tagline remain readable. Use the emblem at small sizes.
Do not place the detailed emblem over busy photography or low-contrast backgrounds.
Do not add a second shadow, outline, badge shape, or competing gradient around the artwork.
4 Mobile launcher icon and splash screen

The launcher icon should use the Ascend mountain A as the focal symbol. Start from the full-color emblem, simplify fine brush and ring details where necessary, and place it on a solid Ink or warm cream background. Do not include the Ascend wordmark or tagline inside the launcher icon because they will be unreadable at notification and home-screen sizes.
Create a 1024 x 1024 square master. Keep the artwork inside generous optical margins and let the system apply the final icon mask.
Provide separate foreground and background layers at 108 x 108 dp. Keep essential detail inside the centered 66 x 66 dp safe zone.
Use a clean single-color mountain A derived from the monochrome emblem for themed icons.
Export a dedicated 512 x 512 store icon from the approved launcher artwork.
Use a simplified solid silhouette. Avoid the wordmark, ring ornament, gradients, and fine brush texture.

Center the primary emblem on a solid warm page background. Keep the first screen quiet and fast: one emblem, no tagline animation, and no extra onboarding copy. Match the first rendered application screen background so the transition feels continuous.
Verify the icon at 16, 24, 32, 48, and 60 logical pixels.
Confirm the central A remains recognizable under circle, squircle, rounded-square, and OEM masks.
Confirm the black mountain does not disappear against dark system surfaces.
Review light, dark, tinted, and themed variants on real devices where supported.

The product interface uses warm neutral surfaces with terracotta actions. Gold belongs to the identity and decorative brand moments; it should not replace accessible semantic colors for success, warning, danger, or information.
Logo detail and limited brand accent
Secondary accent and calm status context
Use Geist when bundled; otherwise use the platform system sans serif for native controls and dense UI.
Use sparingly for marketing, About, and narrative headings. Do not use for workout data entry.
Use for fixed-width values only when alignment materially improves scanning.
Meet WCAG AA contrast for text and interactive controls.
Never rely on color alone to communicate state; pair it with a label, icon, or shape change.
Support dynamic type and text scaling without clipping the word Ascend or essential actions.
Provide meaningful accessibility labels for brand images used as navigation links; use decorative semantics when the same nearby text already names the brand.

Ascend is a fitness coaching platform for athletes and coaches. It brings training plans, workout logging, progress tracking, nutrition, coach-client collaboration, competitions, and evidence-led insights into one connected training record.
Plan training, log every set, track progress, and work with a coach in Ascend.

Ascend là nền tảng huấn luyện thể chất dành cho người tập và huấn luyện viên. Ứng dụng kết nối kế hoạch tập, nhật ký từng set, theo dõi tiến độ, dinh dưỡng, cộng tác giữa huấn luyện viên và học viên, giải đấu và các phân tích dựa trên dữ liệu trong cùng một hồ sơ tập luyện.
Keep in English inside supplied artwork

Use direct, practical language. Explain what happened, what the athlete can do next, and why it matters. Avoid exaggerated promises, generic motivation, or language that implies medical diagnosis. Ascend Coach should sound like a perceptive training partner grounded in the athlete's available data.
Replace Xenoh anywhere it is visible to a user. Search case-insensitively across source code, localization files, bundled content, screenshots, tests, and release metadata.
Set the installed app name and store title to Ascend.
Replace legacy artwork with the approved Ascend icon family.
Use the Ascend emblem or horizontal lockup and Ascend accessibility labels.
Replace visible Xenoh wordmarks and labels with Ascend.
Update welcome copy, value proposition, permissions rationale, and illustrations.
Update About, legal, privacy, delete-account, support, and sign-out context.
Use Ascend Library, Ascend Coach, and Ascend athlete consistently.
Update notification titles, categories, channel descriptions, and default icons.
Show Ascend in password reset, verification, deletion, and social sign-in flows.
Update labels, icons, empty states, and accessibility descriptions.
Update title, descriptions, screenshots, preview media, promotional text, and release notes.
Replace the brand name while keeping currently valid support addresses and URLs.
Update human-readable event and property labels without breaking event contracts.

Search for Xenoh, xenoh, XENOH, spaced lettering such as X E N O H, legacy image filenames, accessibility labels, notification text, email subjects, test fixtures, and screenshots containing the old mark.

The brand migration and the technical-identifier migration are separate releases. The mobile rebrand must not break authentication, persisted sessions, analytics, deep links, networking, or backend contracts.
API and asset domains using xenoh.online or xenoh.app
They are live network locations and contact addresses.
Custom URL schemes such as xenoh://
External authentication callbacks and existing links may depend on them.
The backend analytics contract currently expects these names.
Local storage, secure storage, and preference keys containing xenoh
Renaming without migration can sign users out or discard preferences.
JWT issuer, audience, cookie, Redis, database, bucket, and cache identifiers
Changing them requires coordinated backend and infrastructure deployment.
They are internal implementation identifiers and do not appear in the mobile UI.
Payment matching logic may depend on the exact format.
If technical identifiers are renamed later
Define old-to-new compatibility behavior for every key, scheme, header, and endpoint.
Release backend support for both identifiers before the mobile client switches.
Migrate persisted mobile data without losing sessions, preferences, or queued work.
Keep legacy deep links and authentication callbacks operational during the support window.
Monitor failures by app version and remove compatibility only after active legacy clients fall below the approved threshold.

The supplied PNG files have transparent backgrounds. Before mobile release, create platform-ready derivatives with documented backgrounds, optical padding, color profiles, and export settings. Keep the supplied originals unchanged as source artwork.

[ ] Ascend Coach, Ascend Library, and Ascend athlete use approved capitalization.
[ ] No old logo appears in screens, widgets, shortcuts, notifications, screenshots, or preview media.

[ ] Light, dark, tinted, and themed icon variants are reviewed where supported.

English and Vietnamese naming matches this guide across app, notifications, email-linked screens, and stores.
The mountain A remains clear, centered, and unclipped across required platform masks and sizes.
Brand assets and controls remain readable, labeled, scalable, and contrast compliant.
